finding.statement: Muskett's Suffolk Manorial Families grounds the English network behind the 1627 letter: Brampton Gurdon married Muriel, a Sedley-of-Morley and Knyvett-of-Ashwelthorpe granddaughter, and the 1591 will of Martha Heigham of Denham names Martha Lewkenor (the future Mrs. Gurney) among the Denham Lewkenor daughters and endows an Emmanuel College scholarship — the Denham puritan-gentry matrix. No early-modern Gurney appears anywhere in the volume; the Gurdon–Gurney link runs solely through the Sedley/Lewkenor channel.

dates.display: 3 October 1605 (deaths of Sir Edward Lewkenor and Susan (Heigham) of Denham)

outgoing.explanation: The Winthrop family's personal memorial of Martha (Lewkenor) Gurney's parents in 1605 shows the senior branch's Denham kin standing inside the Winthrops' own circle a generation before the 1627 letter, deepening the documented tie between the branch and the Massachusetts founders.

finding.shortLabel: Adam Winthrop's diary records the 1605 deaths of Martha (Lewkenor) Gurney's Denham parents

sources.alignmentNote: Adam Winthrop's diary entry naming the 1605 deaths of the Denham Lewkenors, Martha (Lewkenor) Gurney's parents.
sources.locator: Winthrop Papers, vol. I, p. 153 (Adam Winthrop's diary/almanac, 3 Oct. 1605)

finding.statement: Adam Winthrop - John Winthrop's father - recorded in his diary the deaths of Sir Edward Lewkenor of Denham and his wife on 3 October 1605: 'Sir Edwarde Lewkenor of Denham in Suff[olk] Knight died of the smalpocks. Vir bonus et doctus fuit et patriae amans. The lady his wife died 2 dayes before him.' The couple were Sir Edward Lewkenor (d. 1605) and Susan (Heigham), the parents of Martha (Lewkenor) Gurney - so the Winthrop family personally memorialised the widowed Mrs. Gurney's own parents, in warm terms, a generation before the 1627 Gurdon-Winthrop letter carried a Gurney suit to John Winthrop's chamber.
